neighbours.label: anatomical adjective that makes ' tract' the expected next word (gastrointestinal, respiratory, urinary, digestive, …)
fire: Doctors found a small ulcer in the lining of the patient's gastrointestinal tract during the examination.
Smoking irritates the cells that line the lower respiratory tract and makes infections more likely.
Women are more prone than men to infections of the urinary tract, especially after surgery.
Fibre passes through most of the digestive tract without being broken down by enzymes.
The virus first multiplies in the cells of the upper respiratory tract before spreading to the lungs.
Some antibiotics upset the natural bacteria of the gastrointestinal tract and cause cramps.
Kidney stones can block the flow of urine at several points along the urinary tract.
In cattle, the parasite settles in the walls of the intestinal tract and feeds on blood.
quiet: Doctors found a small clot in one of the vessels of the patient's cardiovascular system during the examination.
Smoking damages the cells of the immune system and makes infections more likely.
Women are more prone than men to disorders of the thyroid gland, especially after pregnancy.
Calcium is stored mostly in the bones of the skeletal system and released when needed.
The virus first attacks the cells of the central nervous system before spreading to the muscles.
Some antibiotics upset the balance of the lymphatic system and cause swelling.
Blood clots can block the flow of blood at several points along the coronary arteries.
In cattle, the parasite settles in the muscles of the hind legs and feeds on tissue.

notes: Card: ' gastrointestinal' x5 of top 32, plus ' a' before 'tragic'; the output direction suppresses ' tract', ' trace', ' tragic', ' trunc' (tr- words). Probes: gastrointestinal 0.68, respiratory 0.68, urinary 0.42, 'a tragic hero' 0.24. The wider pattern may be 'a tr- word is expected next'; this test claims only the tract case. Near misses use body-system adjectives that take 'system', not 'tract'.
